Beállítom Alig két hónap után leváltották Ruszin-Szendi Romulusz honvédelmi miniszter kabinetfőnökét. A Hvg.hu cikke szerint nem sok ideig maradhatott a poszton Stefán Attila, aki korábban Ruszin-Szendi választási kampányát segítette a hajdúszoboszlói (Hajdú-Bihar 5) választókerületben. A kabinetet egy ideje Beluzsárné Belicza Andrea vezeti, aki sajtófőnökként kezdett a miniszter stábjában, és korábban a Pest Megyei Rendőr-főkapitányság szóvivője volt. A Honvédelmi Minisztérium azt megerősítette a lapnak, hogy a kabinetfőnöki feladatokat jelenleg Beluzsárné látja el, ám azt tagadták, hogy Stefán Attila valaha is betöltötte volna ezt a posztot. Ennek ugyanakkor ellentmond, hogy Stefánt maga Ruszin-Szendi nevezte meg kabinetfőnökeként a május 24-én közzétett videójában, és Stefán több hivatalos eseményen is feltűnt a miniszter kíséretében. Mi is úgy értesültünk, hogy Stefán volt a miniszter kabinetfőnöke, bizalmasa. A Hvg.hu információi szerint Stefán kinevezésére magasabb szintről mondhattak nemet, de a minisztérium válasza szerint „a munkájára a jövőben is számítanak”. Azt nem árulták el, hogy hol, a lap azonban kiszúrta, hogy Stefán nemrég a HM Elektronikai, Logisztikai és Vagyonkezelő Zrt. telephelyére látogató Ruszin-Szendi mellett tűnt fel ismét , a korábbi képekkel szemben már nem az első sorban. A minisztérium alá tartozó cég vezérigazgatója a lap kérdésére csak annyit közölt, hogy a munkavállalók személyiségi jogainak védelme érdekében nem adhat ki személyes adatokat. Stefánnak nem volt katonai múltja, a civil világból érkezett, Ruszin-Szendi szerint „az összes előnyével és hátrányával, amit a civil életből lehet hozni”. https://www.dw.com/en/germany-says-russi.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JjRN The airport is ​a cargo and military logistics hub used by NATO and Ukraine's Antonov Airlines for military supplies Image: Hendrik Schmidt/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement The German government on Tuesday said Russia was "responsible" for an attempted drone attack at the Leipzig/Halle Airport on August 4. "The federal government concludes that Russia is responsible for the hybrid attack in Leipzig," said Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt at a press conference in Berlin on Tuesday afternoon, adding that the attack fitted the pattern of a "long series of destabilization operations" against Europe. Leipzig airport attack: What has Germany said? "The means used — such as the drone configuration, components, explosives and detonation systems — are known to us from other hybrid operations by Russia and its war against Ukraine," added Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul. Authorities discovered a drone fitted with explosives and a detonation mechanism on the evening of August 4 in the security area of Leipzig/Halle Airport between Ukrainian cargo aircraft and believe a second drone may have collided with a DHL aircraft nearby. Last week, German media reported a third drone, also loaded with explosives, had also been discovered at the airport. German federal prosecutors described the incident as a "serious attack on Germany's transport and logistics infrastructure." "Taken together, police investigations, patterns of the crime and intelligence findings substantiate Russian responsibility for the attempted attack at Leipzig Airport," said Dobrindt. Over the weekend, German chancellor Friedrich Merz had promised that a formal response to the incident would be made public in the coming days. He did not go into further detail but said that Germany's European Union and NATO allies would "not be surprised." Earlier on Tuesday, Foreign Minister Wadephul vowed a measured response to the discovery of the drone, but stopped short of holding Russia directly responsible for the incident until his press conference with Interior Minister Dobrindt. EU top diplomat points finger at Russia The European Union's foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas said earlier on Tuesday that it was "clear" that Russia was involved in the drone incident, but declined to comment further until Germany had identified those it believes were responsible, Kallas said Russia was becoming increasingly provocative, raising the question of what could be done to deter Moscow from escalating tensions any further. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text: Pope Leo XIV visited the Peruvian Amazon on Sunday and warned that environmental destruction was threatening the rainforest and the people who depend on it. Photograph: John Reyes Mejia/EPA View image in fullscreen Pope Leo XIV visited the Peruvian Amazon on Sunday and warned that environmental destruction was threatening the rainforest and the people who depend on it. Photograph: John Reyes Mejia/EPA Pope Leo XIV ‘The blood of these brothers cries out’: Pope Leo demands justice for people killed protecting the Amazon Pontiff delivers forceful speech in Peru as he travels from high in the Andes into the Amazon Dan Collyns and Associated Press Sun 15 Nov 2026 20.13 EST Last modified on Mon 16 Nov 2026 01.45 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Pope Leo XIV has demanded justice for environmental defenders killed for protecting the Amazon and backed efforts by Indigenous peoples to stop their lands from being ravaged by logging and illegal mining. On the penultimate day of his South American tour, Leo on Sunday travelled into the Peruvian Amazon and channelled one of Pope Francis’s core teachings that links care for the most vulnerable with care for God’s creation. “The cry of the Earth and the cry of the poor are inseparable,” Leo told Indigenous representatives and missionaries gathered along the Ucayali River in the north-eastern city of Pucallpa. Pope Leo gets rapturous welcome on return to Peru: ‘This visit is like a big party’ Read more He said he came to Pucallpa to support them in their search for justice and peace and referred to what environmental groups estimate have been 57 murders of environmental defenders between 2010 and 2024. “The blood of these brothers cries out to God and demands justice,” Leo said to applause from the crowd, many of whom were wearing traditional feathered headwear and face markings of the region. In addition to deforestation, illegal gold mining has become an increasingly lucrative business in the Amazon, devastating forests and polluting rivers. Illegal mining and coca production has also driven deforestation . Leo addressed the combination of threats in one of his most forceful speeches to date, drawing on his years of experience as a Peruvian bishop and Francis’s constant preaching about the environment and the plight of Indigenous groups. View image in fullscreen Pope Leo greets a child while arriving on the popemobile to celebrate mass at the Villa Deportiva Regional Ucayali in Peru’s Amazon region. Photograph: Yara Nardi/Reuters During the encounter and a subsequent mass in Pucallpa, he demanded a different model of economic development that respects the Earth and the Indigenous peoples who care for it, rather than the “irresponsible exploitation” by outside actors. “Very little has been done – and very slowly at that – while the means to exploit and pollute creation have accelerated,” he said at mass. “In the face of these evils, let us not bury the Lord’s gifts, for he gives us the strength to repair and heal the suffering caused by an insatiable thirst for domination.” In Peru, most murders of environmental defenders go unpunished; only a few have resulted in convictions. The most recent conviction came in the case of Kichwa leader Quinto Inuma Alvarado, who was murdered in 2023 when he was ambushed by hitmen on a river in the San Martín region, the Amazonian territory he was defending. Leo also referred to a notorious rise in sexual violence against Indigenous Awajún and Wampis schoolgirls in the northern Amazon, and blasted the “impunity” and “corruption” surrounding them. The Awajún and Wampis Women’s Council has recorded 370 cases of sexual violence in the Condorcanqui province between January and July. Julio Cusurichi, an Indigenous leader, handed Leo a letter during his visit to Pucallpa, asking him to help protect the rights of uncontacted Indigenous relatives. “The Peruvian state is weakening the mechanisms that should safeguard their territories,” said the letter from the Indigenous rights organisation Aidesep, on which Cusurichi is a board member. “We cannot allow economic interests to take precedence over the lives and rights of these vulnerable peoples. Therefore, we ask Pope Leo XIV to raise his voice and support this urgent call for their defence.” Cardinal Pedro Barreto praised the pope’s decision to meet with Indigenous peoples. Barreto, a former Peruvian archbishop who helped win a multimillion-dollar pollution payout for an Andean town, said: “[Leo] is well aware of all the historical suffering … corruption, illegal mining, deforestation, and the contempt shown by politicians.” Luis E Fernandez, co-founder of Cincia, a scientific research centre in Peru, also hailed the pontiff’s power to raise awareness. “Pope Leo’s recognition of pollution from illegal mining brings much-needed attention to a crisis affecting Indigenous and riverine communities across the Amazon,” he said. Fernandez visited the Vatican in October and presented Leo with scientific evidence detailing the impact of illegal gold mining and associated mercury poisoning. Pope Leo XIV rides in helicopter cockpit with Peruvian air force pilots Leo’s last full day in Peru was also his most ambitious, crisscrossing the nation to minister to communities high in the Andes mountains. Peru’s air force released footage of the pope inside a helicopter and said it was “an unforgettable memory” to take Leo around the country. His first stop was the mountain city of Cusco, where huge crowds greeted him. “It is all worth it,” said Margarida Salomon, 63, who said she came from Sucre in Bolivia to see the pontiff, spending about $500 to take a bus and sleep in a tent. “I am still getting to know this pope, but the fact he is here in the Andes means a lot.” The visit to Cusco, 3,400m (more than 11,000ft) above sea level, tested Leo’s stamina as he continues recovering from lung cancer surgery last month. Leo sat in the chair of his popemobile during part of the ride around Cusco, but it wasn’t clear if that was to preserve his energy or to steady himself on the uneven streets. In general, the 71-year-old Leo has seemed unfazed by the toll of the three-nation South American trip , the longest of his pontificate. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/11/22/tome.text: Tömegverekedés tört ki Nyíregyházán, a Nyíregyháza Spartacus FC és a Debrecen DVSC szurkolói között – derül ki a rendőrség közléséből. A két csapat NB I.-es rangadója előtt vasárnap délután összecsapott két nagyobb csoport a nyíregyházi stadionhoz közel eső egyik utcában. A rendőrség azt írta, hogy a verekedést gyorsan megállították, és a környéket továbbra is biztosítják. A mentőszolgálat munkatársai több sérültet kórházba vittek. A hatóságok csoportos garázdaság gyanúja miatt fognak előállítani és elszámoltatni több embert is. A Szon.hu szerint eltérnek a debreceni és a nyíregyházi szurkolók beszámolói. Az előbbiek szerint ötvenen „megtámadtak egy kocsmát”, ahol a rivális csapat szurkolói voltak. Szerintük egyeseknél kések, botok és vascsövek is voltak, és nyolc-tíz percen át zajlott a csetepaté. A közösségi médiában keringő videókon valóban volt, akinek a kezében bot volt. A nyíregyházi ultrák szerint viszont nem volt eszköz senkinél, három-négy percig tartott az összecsapás, aztán a debreceniek elfutottak.
